explicit_exclusions.PIL: No manifest or CI requirement; existing try/except ImportError provides a genuine PNG fallback, so not allowlisted.
explicit_exclusions.build: examples/scenario_lab/verify.py resolves same-directory build.py; CI build distribution is unrelated and must not justify ignoring this internal import.
explicit_exclusions._checks/build_demo_db/corpus/run_validat: Internal script or namespace imports, not external dependencies.

limitations_and_guards: ignored-modules is not no-parse and cannot verify missing third-party APIs in a dependency-free service. CI installs declared dependencies, runs strict typing, tests, and wheel checks.

Relative ImportFrom passes its unqualified module to the ignore matcher, so from .pytest import absent is masked by ignored-modules=pytest. This observed limitation requires a repository AST guard against any relative import whose first module component is allowlisted.

Bare script imports can refer to same-directory modules. A repository AST guard rejects allowlisted names that resolve to script/example sibling .py files or package directories. Package-qualified siblings such as sqlseed_ai.mcp do not shadow external top-level imports.
Allowlist entries must be exact top-level identifiers, never glob patterns or internal source package names; every entry has a manifest or CI lock distribution mapping.
All commands run from repository root, matching CI. Relative init-hook/source-roots paths are not portable to arbitrary cwd; no unreliable __file__ or Pylint-private globals are used.
The configuration does not disable E0401, E0611 or an import checker/category and does not change rule thresholds/source ignores.
